correctness.rationale: The forward reflexive diamond of any nonempty subset is the initial segment ending at its rightmost world. A tuple of k generator subsets assigns each world a k-bit color. Terms preserve unions of maximal consecutive constant-color runs. Nested color tests separated by future diamond distinguish any earlier run from each later run: adjacent tested colors differ so each test needs a distinct successive run. Hence the generated Boolean algebra has exactly those run atoms. Taking the atoms of any diamond-stable subalgebra as initial generators proves all subalgebra atoms are consecutive intervals and the lattice is Boolean on n-1 cut positions. Color words with exactly r runs count as m*C(n-1,r-1)*(m-1)^(r-1), m=2^k; independent adjacent equality indicators lead to Z~Bin(n-1,1/m), full-generation probability (1-1/m)^(n-1), and the stated Poisson window. Single alternating generator achieves full generation for n>=2; n=1 needs zero. Independent direct Boolean term closure verified 1,431 generator color words with n<=5,k<=2, and checked all 278 set partitions through n=6 against the interval criterion.
